title: Build the application shell and mode indicators
work: Create the context bar, candidate rail, genome area, task graph area and evidence drawer. Build against labeled fixtures immediately.
done: Assembly, cell context, selected candidate and LIVE / RECORDED / MOCK status remain visible throughout navigation.

title: Build the coordinate-correct genome overview
work: Render chromosome bars from actual lengths and candidate markers from actual intervals. Use neutral unexplored background and clear selection.
done: Marker placement is mathematically tied to genomic position, not decorative spacing. Selecting a marker selects the same candidate everywhere.

title: Integrate the locus browser
work: Use igv.js for candidate boundaries, the exact annotation release and computed features. Verify reference configuration, offsets and asset access early.
done: Displayed coordinates and features match backend calculations. Convenient default annotations must not silently replace the computed release.

title: Build the reference-base strip
work: Render a short frozen sequence window with coordinate ticks, readable bases and candidate highlighting. Preserve reference orientation and label strand-specific transformations explicitly.
done: Displayed bases match the artifact bytes and genomic offsets. No decorative random DNA appears in a scientific view.

title: Connect overview, chromosome, locus and sequence zoom
work: Create a shared viewport state containing assembly, chromosome, interval, selection and zoom level. Transition between representations without losing the selected locus.
done: Users can zoom in and back out with consistent coordinates and breadcrumbs. Respect available data boundaries.

title: Build candidate conclusions and comparison cards
work: Show criterion status, endpoint support, freshness and the most consequential unresolved question. Keep workflow progress separate from scientific interpretation.
done: A viewer understands the current conclusion without reading genomic tracks. No unexplained safety score or fake precision appears.

title: Build the stable investigation DAG
work: Use React Flow in read-only mode. Group tasks into readable stages, preserve positions through updates and expand on demand.
done: Real dependencies, shared inputs and reopened work are visible. Node interactions reveal actual task records.

title: Build evidence and numerical-result inspection
work: Show source versions, biological context, original table rows, calculations, supporting assessments and limitations. Link a result back to its genomic location.
done: A judge can move from conclusion to evidence to original numeric input within a few clicks.

title: Implement the event reducer and reconnect behavior
work: Apply ordered upserts, deduplicate event IDs and recover sequence gaps using snapshots or missing event pages.
done: Refresh, reconnect and duplicate delivery do not corrupt state or invent task completion.

title: Implement deterministic timeline replay
work: Support play, pause, seek, speed control and meaningful-event navigation. Rebuild state from events or versioned replay snapshots.
done: Seeking backward restores earlier assessments and source versions. Final results never leak into an earlier replay frame.

title: Add cinematic genome-follow cues
work: Create a separate cue file keyed to actual event sequences: focus chromosome, zoom locus, show bases, highlight a result, then reveal the relevant graph branch.
done: Playback is smooth and synchronized with real events. Pausing or disabling camera follow leaves the application usable. Cues cannot change scientific state.

title: Build the harness-change comparison drawer
work: Show parent and candidate architecture, a readable policy diff, validation results and promotion/rejection.
done: Judges can identify what changed in execution and what happened to measured performance. Display actual values, including failures.

title: Build the presentation and dossier flow
work: Provide a clean presentation mode, a reset-to-start action and access to the final versioned dossier. Preload the selected replay assets.
done: The entire story can be demonstrated predictably and the exported result agrees with the screen.

title: Verify projection readability and motion behavior
work: Check a 1280×720 presentation viewport, large conclusions, readable stage labels, keyboard interaction, reduced motion and text alternatives to tracks.
done: No critical content requires microscopic text, color discrimination or continuous animation to understand.
